journal:
# Abdullah's BodyTracker journal (p09)

## Day 1 (Sun 2026-10-04)
- Welcome screen was clear. Set up profile: 172 cm, 45 y, 101.4 kg, male, sedentary (desk job). Answered "No / not sure" to "eating at current intake 2+ weeks" because I'm just starting to diet.
- The profile weight showed up as today's weigh-in automatically, good — I didn't have to type 101.4 twice.
- Nutrition screen first said target 2,240 "maintain". I was confused — I want to LOSE. Had to find the ⚙ gear on the Nutrition tab to pick "Lose". Would be nice if the setup asked the goal.
- After picking Lose (0.5%/week default): target 1,870 kcal. The app explained the math gives 1683 but it won't go below my BMR (1869), "expect slower progress". OK, so the app has a floor. Good to know for later.
- Carbs "~330 g" appeared while on Maintain - seemed a lot. Will see what it shows now.
- Maintenance 2,240 ± 530 "Estimated, 0% from your data". Wide range but it says it's honest about that.
- Food log: easy. Label, calories, protein, carbs, fat, Add entry. The first "Add entry" is a heading, the button is the second one — minor.
- Logged 4 meals = 2,009 kcal, ticked "Day complete". Protein 114 g vs 133 g target (1.8 g/kg on a 74 kg "reference weight" — not sure what reference weight is, I weigh 101).
- Decided (plan) to eat ~1,870 from tomorrow, since that's my target.

## Day 2 (Mon)
- Scale 102.3 (up 0.9 from yesterday!). Annoying, but the app showed "Trend weight 101.5" which calmed me down a bit.
- Confusion: I tapped the big "Weight" tile expecting to add a weigh-in, but it opened a "Weight trend" chart. The add button is the smaller "+ Weight" further down. (screens/1790454691806.png)
- Logged 4 meals = 1,695 kcal, day complete. Under target, good.
- Recommendation still says "needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" even though it's my 2nd day — seems it only counts at the weekly update? Slightly confusing.

## Day 3 (Tue)
- Scale 101.6. Home shows "▲ 0.2 kg" — compared with my first weigh-in (101.4), not yesterday (102.3). Took me a second; the "vs First" toggle at top explains it.
- Ate 2,117 — over my 1,870 plan (lunch was big). Logged all, complete.
- Opened "Explain the math →": lots of formulas (Kalman filter, Hall 2008, MAD, Forbes...). Way over my head. The bits I got: the formula says my BMR is 1,869, sedentary maintenance 2,243, and "days 1–7 allow extra water movement" because I said I just started. Useful that it exists, but not written for a normal person. (screens/1790454764332.png)

## Day 4 (Wed)
- Scale 101.3, "▼ 0.1 kg" from start. Trend 101.5. Ate 1,709 (pizza dinner but under target). Average intake shown 1,883.
- Nothing new on screen. Protein note: 123 g avg vs 133 g target.

## Day 5 (Thu)
- Scale 101.0 (▼0.4 from start). Trend 101.4.
- The app warned: "macros add up to ~1287 kcal vs 1515 kcal logged (15% apart). One of the numbers may be off." Nice catch — the cookie package numbers I copied don't add up. I'll leave it; it's what the label says.
- My dinner estimate only had calories and protein. Logged just those; the day total then only shows kcal + protein (carbs/fat total disappears for the day). A bit odd — I'd expect it to show the carbs/fat I did log.
- (My own slip: I ticked "Day complete" before logging dinner, then added dinner afterwards. App accepted it fine.) Day total 2,042.

## Day 6 (Fri)
- Scale 101.2. Trend 101.4. Ate 1,533. Macro mismatch warning again (15%). Protein avg 117 vs 133 — I keep missing the protein target.

## Day 7 (Sat)
- Scale 99.9! Under 100 for the first time in ages. Home shows "▼ 1.5 kg" but "Trend weight 101.3". Part of me wants to believe 99.9, but OK, the app says trend.
- Breakfast oats: I didn't know macros, logged calories only. The entry says "no macros" and the day total now only shows kcal (no protein/carbs/fat at all for the day). Fine but I lose my protein number for the day.
- Ate 1,614.

## Week 1 (review on day 7, Sat 2026-10-10)
- Maintenance shown: 2,240 ± 530 kcal/day, "Estimated", 0% from my data (still the formula). Updated weekly on Sunday; next 2026-10-11.
- Target: 1,870 kcal/day ("lose · 0.5%/wk · at minimum"). The app says the math gives 1683 but it won't go below my BMR 1869, "expect slower progress".
- Recommendation: "Suggested intake 1,870. An on-track check needs 14 days of data."
- Avg intake 1,817 kcal (7/7 days complete). kg/week: "needs data". Protein 117 g vs 133 g target.
- Body composition: "Not enough data yet" (needs 3 BIA readings at each end 21 days apart — I don't have a body-fat scale, just weight).
- What I understand: I'm eating a bit under my target; the app can't yet say if I'm on track. Weight trend 101.4 → 101.3, so barely moving so far, but the app warned me progress will be slow and the check needs 14 days.
- Decision: keep eating ~1,870 (no change). No `plan` change.

## Day 8 (Sun) — weekly update day
- Scale 99.7, trend 101.1. Weekly update ran: maintenance now 2,290 ± 530 (was 2,240), still "Estimated, 0% from your data" — after a full week of complete logging and daily weigh-ins I expected at least a few %. Target unchanged at 1,870 (floor = BMR 1,866).
- From here I use a small routine script in my folder that weighs + logs my meals through the app screens; I check the screens after each batch.

## Days 9–14 (routine)
- Scale: 98.8, 98.0, 97.9 (!!), then 99.4, 100.0, 100.1. Up 2.2 kg in three days even though I ate 1,800–2,040. That hurt. Trend went 100.9 → 100.6 → 100.3 → 100.2 → 100.2 → 100.2.
- Intake 1,800–2,040/day, a bit above my 1,870 plan on some days (pizza, big dinners). All days logged + complete.
- Some dinners (pizza) only had kcal + protein on my estimate; again the day total dropped carbs/fat.

## Week 2 (review on day 14, Sat 2026-10-17)
- Maintenance: 2,290 ± 530 "Estimated", still "0% from your data" (said "typically 3–5 weeks").
- Target 1,870 (lose 0.5%/wk, at minimum = BMR). Recommendation: "Suggested intake 1,870. On-track check needs 14 days of data (day 8 so far)" — it counts from the last weekly update, so it still says day 8 though I've logged 14 days.
- Avg intake 1,898. kg/week (14-day): -1.58 (95%: -2.94 to -0.23). Protein 125 g vs 133 g.
- What I think: the app says I'm losing ~1.5 kg a week?? But the scale went UP 2 kg this week. Confusing — which do I believe? The trend line (100.2) is flat for 3 days. I'm annoyed but it's only 3 days, the app told me water swings happen. Trend is still 1.2 kg below where I started.
- Decision: no change, keep ~1,870. No warning or advice to eat less on screen.

## Day 15 (Sun 2026-10-18) — weekly update
- Scale 100.x, trend 100.2. New recommendation text:
  "Your estimated rate (−1.68 kg to −0.51 kg per week) doesn't include your target of −0.50 kg/week. Eating about 650 kcal/day more than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake: 1,860 kcal/day."
- POSSIBLE BUG / CONTRADICTION: it tells me to eat ~650 kcal MORE than recently, but the suggested intake (1,860) is LOWER than my recent average (1,916 shown right below). So which is it? Eat 2,550 or 1,860? Also −0.51 vs −0.50 is basically my target — splitting hairs to call that "doesn't include". (screens/1790455225717.png)
- Maintenance now 2,240 ± 500, "Estimated, 9% from your data".
- My reaction: I'm NOT going to eat 650 more — my scale just went back up to 100. I'll stick with the suggested number (1,860 ≈ what I planned). No plan change.

## Day 16 (Mon 2026-10-19) — the stall
- Scale 100.0. Honestly the scale hasn't gone anywhere for a week (97.9 was a fluke). I'm frustrated and thinking about going to 1,500 a day.
- Before doing it, I looked at the app:
  - Weight trend chart: the thick trend line went from 101.4 down to ~100.2 and is flat since 10-14. (screens/1790455280401.png)
  - Nutrition still said I'm losing faster than my 0.5% target (−1.09 kg/wk, 95% −1.68 to −0.51) and to eat MORE, not less.
  - I went into ⚙ and changed weekly rate to 1% (the top of "Suggested 0.25–1%") to see if the app would give me a lower number. It didn't: "On track. Your estimated rate (−1.68 to −0.51 kg per week) includes your target of −1 kg/week. Suggested intake: 1,860." And: "The math gives 1137 kcal/day, which is below the minimum this app will suggest (1857 — the larger of your estimated BMR and 1,500)".
- What I understood: the app thinks I'm on track and will not go below ~1,860 no matter what. It never tells me to cut. 1,500 would be below what the app is willing to recommend.
- Decision: I will NOT cut to 1,500. I listen to the app: stay around 1,860. (No plan change.) I left the rate at 1% because "On track" made me feel better.
- Note: the app never actually mentions that my scale weight is stuck — no "plateau" message. It only gives the numbers. For someone like me a sentence like "a flat week is normal, don't cut" would help more than the ranges.

## Days 17–21
- Scale: 100.2, 101.0, 100.4, 100.0, 100.4. Trend stuck at 100.2–100.3 all week. Day 19 I was again thinking of 1,500.
- Intake 1,661–1,846, then 2,334 on Saturday (big mandi dinner out).

## Week 3 (review on day 21, Sat 2026-10-24)
- Maintenance 2,240 ± 500 "Estimated, 9% from your data". Target 1,860 (lose 1%/wk, at minimum).
- Recommendation: "On track. Your estimated rate (−1.68 to −0.51 kg/week) includes your target of −1 kg/week. Suggested 1,860."
- kg/week (14-day): still shows −1.09 — the same number as last Sunday. Weekly figures are frozen until the Sunday update. (screens/1790455478561.png)
- My read: the app says "On track, ~1 kg/week" but my trend line hasn't moved in 10 days (100.2 → 100.3). That feels wrong/out of date. I don't fully trust the "On track" now. But the app still clearly refuses to go below 1,857, so I'm still not going to 1,500. I'll wait for tomorrow's weekly update.
- Decision: no change yet.

## Day 22 (Sun 2026-10-25) — weekly update, still stalled
- Scale 100.0. Still frustrated, still thinking about 1,500.
- Weekly update (with my 1%/wk setting): "Your estimated rate (−0.53 kg to +0.27 kg per week) doesn't include your target of −1 kg/week. Eating about 960 kcal/day less than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake: 1,860 kcal/day." + "The math gives 927 kcal/day, which is below the minimum..." (screens/1790455520312.png)
- PROBLEM (for someone like me): the big bold sentence literally tells me to eat 960 kcal LESS (that's ~900 kcal/day!) and then in the same breath suggests 1,860, which is what I already eat (avg 1,874). The two numbers contradict each other. Last week it was the opposite ("eat 650 more", suggested 1,860). If I only read the first sentence I would have slashed to under 1,000. That's exactly the thing I'm prone to.
- Maintenance dropped: 2,030 ± 440, "29% from your data". So I'm only ~170 below maintenance at 1,860 — that explains the slow loss.
- I realised the 1% was my own greed, so I set the weekly rate back to 0.5%. Then it said: "On track. Your estimated rate (−0.53 to +0.27 kg/week) includes your target of −0.50 kg/week. Suggested 1,860." and "The math gives 1477 kcal/day, which is below the minimum this app will suggest (1857)". kg/week (14-day) now −0.13. (screens/1790455535287.png)
- Honestly "On track" at −0.13 kg/week against a −0.50 target is generous. And "the math gives 1477" is almost my 1,500 idea... tempting.
- DECISION: I don't cut hard. The app keeps saying it will not suggest less than ~1,860 (my BMR), says "expect slower progress", and calls me on track. I'll trust it and stay at ~1,860, and be stricter about actually hitting it. No plan change (my average is already 1,874).

## Days 23–28
- Scale 99.1, 98.8, 99.7, 99.2, 99.9, 99.3. Trend crept 100.1 → 99.8. Days 25 and 28 I was frustrated again and thought about 1,500.
- Intake 1,799–2,240 (life happens), all logged + complete.

## Week 4 (review on day 28, Sat 2026-10-31)
- Maintenance 2,030 ± 440 "Estimated, 29% from your data". Target 1,860 (0.5%/wk, at minimum).
- Recommendation (from last Sunday): "On track. Rate −0.53 to +0.27 kg/wk includes −0.50. Suggested 1,860." kg/week (14-day) −0.13.
- Avg intake 1,967 — about 100 over the target. The app doesn't point this out anywhere; I had to compare the two tiles myself.
- My read: trend finally under 100 (99.8). Slow, but moving. The app keeps saying it won't go below 1,857.
- Decision: `plan 1860` — tighten up to actually eat the target (not a hard cut).

## Day 29 (Sun 2026-11-01) — weekly update
- Scale 98.8. Maintenance now "Measured": 2,150 ± 370 (51% from my data). Target 1,850. "On track" (−0.54 to +0.12 kg/wk). The "Measured" badge makes me trust it a bit more.

## Days 30–32
- Scale 98.4, 97.9, then 96.7 on day 32 — whoosh! Home says "▼ 4.7 kg", trend 99.1. The chart shows the trend line finally bending down. (screens/1790455852326.png) I'm happy. Feels like the stall was just water.
- Day 32 a banner appeared: "It's been 30+ days since your last backup. Your data lives only on this device." I tapped "Back up now" → "Your data" screen → "Full backup (JSON)"; file saved (downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-11-04.json), and it now shows "Last backup: 2026-11-04". Clear and easy. Also noticed "Persistent storage: not granted by the browser" — no idea what that means for me.
- Day 32 recommendation still "On track, suggested 1,850".

## Week 5 (review on day 35, Sat 2026-11-07)
- Scale 97.1, 97.2, 97.4; trend 98.9 → 98.6. 
- Maintenance 2,150 ± 370 "Measured" (51% from my data). Target 1,850 (0.5%/wk, at the minimum). Recommendation (from Nov 1): "On track … Suggested 1,850." Avg intake 1,737. kg/week (14-day) −0.21 (frozen from Sunday).
- My read: the whoosh proves patience worked. Glad I didn't slash to 1,500. The −0.21 kg/week figure is out of date (it's from before the drop).
- Decision: keep 1,860 plan. No change.

## Day 36 (Sun 2026-11-08) — weekly update
- Maintenance jumped to 2,470 ± 310 "Measured" (66% from data) — from 2,150 last week and 2,030 the week before. That's a big swing for something called "Measured". Target now 1,930 (no longer "at minimum"). Rate −0.85 to −0.30 kg/wk (−0.58 center). "On track."
- Macro warning on 11-08 (21% apart) — label numbers again.

## Days 37–42
- Scale 96.9, 96.8, 96.2, 96.1, 96.1, 96.2. Trend 98.3 → 97.5. Steady.
- Intake 1,830–2,052.

## Week 6 (review on day 42, Sat 2026-11-14)
- Maintenance 2,470 ± 310 Measured; target 1,930; "On track (−0.85 to −0.30 kg/wk) includes −0.49. Suggested 1,930." Avg intake ~1,850.
- My read: I'm losing ~0.5 kg/week and the app is letting me eat a bit more. I was surprised maintenance jumped by 300 in one week, but OK.
- Decision: `plan 1930` — follow the suggestion.

## Day 43 (Sun 2026-11-15) — weekly update
- Maintenance 2,510 ± 370, and the badge went BACK from "Measured" to "Estimated" (50% from your data; last week was 66%). Confusing — I thought once it's Measured it stays Measured. More data should mean more "measured", not less. (screens/1790456207278.png)
- Target 1,980. "On track (−1 to −0.32 kg/wk)".

## Days 44–49
- Scale 96.1, 96.4, 96.8, 96.9, 96.5, 95.8. Trend 97.2 → 96.9. Day 46 a big day (2,395).

## Week 7 (review on day 49, Sat 2026-11-21)
- Maintenance 2,510 ± 370 "Estimated" (50%). Target 1,980. Recommendation "On track, suggested 1,980". Avg intake 1,922. kg/week −0.66.
- My read: good, steady. But after the stall I'm a bit scared to eat more — the 50 kcal difference doesn't matter.
- Decision: stay at my 1,930 plan (no change).

## Days 50–56
- Scale 95.5, 95.6, 95.7, 96.4, 95.9, 95.2, 95.4. Trend 96.8 → 96.3.
- Day 50 weekly update: maintenance 2,550 ± 340, back to "Measured" (59%). Target 2,030. "On track (−0.92 to −0.31 kg/wk)". Macro mismatch warning again (label numbers).
- Protein average slipped to 112 g vs 133 g.

## Week 8 (review on day 56, Sat 2026-11-28)
- Maintenance 2,550 ± 340 Measured; target 2,030; recommendation "On track, suggested 2,030". Avg intake ~1,985. kg/week −0.61.
- The badge flips Measured → Estimated → Measured week to week. I'm getting used to ignoring it.
- Decision: `plan 2030`. I've lost ~5 kg on the scale since the start and the app keeps telling me I'm on track, so I'll eat what it suggests.

## Days 57–63
- Scale 96.0, 94.7, 94.8, 94.7, 95.1, 95.5, 94.7. Trend 96.2 → 95.6. First time under 95 on the scale!
- Day 57 update: maintenance 2,520 ± 310 Measured (66%), target 2,000, "On track (−0.88 to −0.32)". Protein average dropping (108 g vs 133 g) — the app mentions it but I don't really know how to fix it; it just states the number.

## Week 9 (review on day 63, Sat 2026-12-05)
- Maintenance 2,520 ± 310 Measured; target 2,000; "On track, suggested 2,000". Avg intake 2,094; kg/week −0.60.
- My read: I'm eating a bit over the new target. Fine, still losing.
- Decision: `plan 2000`.

## Days 64–70
- Scale 94.6, 94.3, 94.6, 94.0, 93.9, 94.3, 93.5. Trend 95.5 → 94.8.
- Day 64 update: maintenance 2,580 ± 280 Measured (71%), target 2,070, "On track (−0.85 to −0.32)".
- Backup reminder came back on day 64 (30+ days since 11-04). I did it on day 70: downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-12-12.json. Data screen: 70 weigh-ins, 280 food entries, 70 complete days.

## Week 10 (review on day 70, Sat 2026-12-12)
- Maintenance 2,580 ± 280 Measured; target 2,070; "On track, suggested 2,070"; avg intake ~2,000; kg/week −0.59.
- My read: this is working. Maintenance keeps creeping up each week (2,030 → 2,580 over 7 weeks) — so the app was too low early on; that's why it felt like I was starving and not moving.
- Decision: `plan 2070`.

## Days 71–77
- Scale 93.7, 93.9, 93.8, 93.4, 93.8, 93.9, 93.8. Stuck around 93.8 all week; trend 94.7 → 94.3.
- Day 71 update: maintenance 2,620 ± 270 Measured (75%), target 2,110, "On track (−0.79 to −0.29)".

## Week 11 (review on day 77, Sat 2026-12-19)
- Maintenance 2,620 ± 270 Measured; target 2,110; "On track, suggested 2,110". Avg intake 1,864 (I ate under). kg/week −0.54. Protein 111 g vs 133 g.
- My read: the scale sat still again this week. Old me would panic and cut. But I learned from the October stall — it came off in a whoosh. The app still says on track and suggests MORE, not less.
- Decision: no hard cut, but I'm not raising to 2,110 either — keeping my 2,070 plan. (No plan change.)

## Days 78–84
- Scale 94.1, 94.7, 94.1, 93.5, 93.2, 93.1, 93.6. Trend 94.3 → 94.0. Home: "▼ 7.8 kg" vs first weigh-in.
- Day 78 update: maintenance 2,600 ± 240 Measured (80%), target 2,090, "On track (−0.84 to −0.40)". Protein keeps sliding (103–106 g vs 133 g).

## Week 12 (review on day 84, Sat 2026-12-26)
- Maintenance 2,600 ± 240 Measured (80% from data); target 2,090; "On track, suggested 2,090"; avg intake 1,860; kg/week −0.62.
- Decision: keep going as I am.

## End tasks
- ⇩ → "Your data": 84 weigh-ins, 336 food entries, 84 complete days. Made a Full backup (downloads/bodytracker-backup-2026-12-26.json) and "Export daily data (JSON)", All data (downloads/bodytracker-daily_2026-10-04_to_2026-12-26.json).
- Opened them: both are JSON text. The daily export is readable — one block per day with weight, calories, protein/carbs/fat, complete. But it says "for spreadsheets" and it's JSON — I'd need someone to convert it for Excel. There are separate Weights CSV / Food CSV buttons, which is what I'd actually use.
- In the daily export, days where one meal had no carbs/fat (e.g. 2026-10-08) show only calories + protein, and 2026-12-25 shows only calories, even though most meals that day had macros. Same as in the app's day total. So partial macros silently disappear.

## Final review
What helped: logging was quick, the day-complete tick is simple, and the trend weight line saved my sanity — the thick line is what I learned to look at instead of the daily number. Most important: when I was stuck at 100 kg for three weeks and wanted to drop to 1,500, the app would simply not give me a number below ~1,860 ("the minimum this app will suggest … your BMR") and kept saying "On track". I listened, didn't crash-diet, and the weight came off in a whoosh in early November. 101.4 → 93.6 on the scale (trend 94.0) in 12 weeks.
What confused me: the two weekly messages that said "eat about 650 kcal MORE" and later "eat about 960 kcal LESS than recently" while the "Suggested intake" beside it was basically what I was already eating. The "960 less" line is dangerous for someone like me — if I'd only read that, I'd have eaten 900 a day. Also: the "Measured/Estimated" badge flipping back and forth, the "needs 14 days (day 8 so far)" counter, weekly numbers that stay frozen all week even when the scale clearly changed, "Weight" tile vs "+ Weight" button, and the Explain-the-math page full of formulas.
Complaints: no plain sentence ever says "your weight is flat, this is normal water, don't cut" — I had to piece that together from the floor message. Maintenance moved from 2,030 to 2,620 over the weeks, so early on the app had me eating less than needed. Protein target I never hit and the app just repeats the number without tips.
Would I keep using it: yes.

# p09 (Abdullah, 45, 172 cm, 101 kg, lose) - final report

## 1. Usage
- Used the app on all 84 of 84 days (2026-10-04 to 2026-12-26).
- 336 meals logged (4 a day). All 84 days were marked complete. 84 weigh-ins (the first one came from the profile).
- Scale went from 101.4 to 93.6 kg (▼7.8). The trend line went from 101.4 to 94.0.

## 3. Confusions
- Setup: the goal is never asked. The target showed "maintain" until I found ⚙ on the Nutrition tab and picked Lose.
- Body tab: tapping the big "Weight" tile opens the trend chart. The add button is the smaller "+ Weight".
- Recommendation: "needs 14 days of data (day 1 so far)" stayed "day 1" through day 7, and showed "day 8" on day 14. It only counts at the weekly update.
- Recommendation: "eat 650 kcal MORE" on day 15 and "eat 960 kcal LESS" on day 22, each next to a suggested intake that was about what I already ate.
- Maintenance label: flipped from Measured (66%) to Estimated (50%) to Measured (59%) over 3 weeks.
- Weekly figures (kg/week, rate, "On track") stay frozen all week. It said "On track, −1.09 kg/wk" while my trend was flat for 10 days, and showed −0.21 after the 3 kg whoosh.
- Explain the math: Kalman filter, Hall 2008, MAD and so on. None of it makes sense to a normal user.
- Food log: when one meal has no carbs or fat, the day total drops those macros for the whole day. On a "no macros" meal day it drops protein too.
- Data screen: "Persistent storage: not granted by the browser" with no explanation. The daily export says "for spreadsheets" but comes out as JSON.
- No plain "plateau is normal, don't cut" message during a multi-week stall.

## 4. Possible bugs
1. **The "kcal more/less" text contradicts the suggested intake.**
   - Steps: day 15 (2026-10-18) weekly update. Average intake was 1,916 and the estimated rate was faster than the 0.5% target.
   - Expected: the suggested intake matches the advised change (about 2,550), or the text explains the minimum floor.
   - Actual: "Eating about 650 kcal/day more than recently would close the gap. Suggested intake: 1,860 kcal/day." (screens/1790455225717.png)
   - Opposite case: day 22 at the 1%/wk rate said "about 960 kcal/day less… Suggested 1,860" with average intake about 1,874 (screens/1790455520312.png).
   - This is dangerous for crash-dieters: 960 less means about 900 kcal/day.
2. **Partial macros disappear.**
   - Steps: log meals where one entry has kcal only, or kcal + protein only (days 5, 7, 31, 83).
   - Expected: the day total sums the macros that were entered.
   - Actual: the day total and the daily export leave out carbs/fat, and sometimes protein, for the whole day. For example, the 2026-10-08 export has only calories + protein, and 2026-12-25 has only calories. (screens/1790454864427.png)
3. **Measured/Estimated goes backwards.**
   - Steps: weekly updates on days 36, 43 and 50.
   - Expected: the data share grows as more data comes in.
   - Actual: 66% "Measured" → 50% "Estimated" → 59% "Measured". (screens/1790456207278.png)
   - This may be by design, but it looks broken.
4. **"On track" is generous.**
   - Steps: day 22 at 0.5%/wk.
   - Actual: "On track" with a centre estimate of −0.13 kg/wk against a −0.50 target, only because the 95% range (−0.53 to +0.27) just touches it. (screens/1790455535287.png)
   - Minor.

## 5. Review
The trend line and the app's refusal to go below my BMR are what stopped me crash-dieting when I was stuck at 100 kg for three weeks. I held on, the weight came off, and I'm down almost 8 kg. What I hated was the weekly sentence telling me to eat "650 more" and then "960 less" when the suggested number beside it said something else. Someone like me could easily read only the first line and starve himself. It also never just says in plain words "a flat week is normal, don't cut".

Would keep using: **yes**
